title: DAX Fundamentals: Row vs Filter Context, SUMX & CALCULATE
summary: Understand the twin hearts of DAX evaluation: Row Context (iterating row by row) vs Filter Context (visual slicing via `CALCULATE`).
learningObjectives: Choose correctly between column aggregators (`SUM`) vs row iterators (`SUMX`) inside measures
Use `CALCULATE`, `ALL`, `ALLSELECTED`, and `VAR` cleanly to modify filter contexts deterministically
prerequisiteConcepts: Star Schema and Date modeling fundamentals

sections.heading: 1. Mastering Filter Context vs Row Context
sections.content:
Every DAX headache comes from confusing two contexts: **Filter Context** comes from report slicers, matrix rows/columns, and active relationships narrowing down rows *before* aggregation (`SUM` has no row context!). **Row Context** steps row-by-row when evaluating Computed Columns OR X-suffix iterators (`SUMX`, `AVERAGEX`).

Meanwhile, **`CALCULATE(expr, filter1, ...)`** is DAX's superpower—it can overwrite, add, or strip active visual slicers cleanly (e.g., stripping `Region` filter via `ALL(DimRegion)` to calculate reliable `% Share of Global Revenue`).

codeExamples.code:
Visual Slicer (Year = 2026) + Matrix Row (Region = North)
   |--> Filter Context narrows FactSales strictly to (2026 AND North)!
   |--> [Measure: Revenue] computes SUM inside narrowed subset!
   |--> [Measure: % Total] uses CALCULATE([Revenue], ALL(Region)) stripping Region ONLY!
codeExamples.explanation: CALCULATE + ALL lets percentage denominators look outside the current matrix row while honoring outer page slicers.

keyPoints: Store reusable sub-calculations inside `VAR ... RETURN` blocks—easier to debug and skips redundant storage engine scans!
Always wrap `/` divisions inside `DIVIDE(num, den, alternate)` preventing ugly `#DIV/0!` or `Infinity` cards.
commonMistakes: Writing `SUM(Sales[Qty] * Sales[Price])` inside a Measure (invalid syntax!) instead of `SUMX(Sales, Sales[Qty] * Sales[Price])`.

sections.heading: 2. % Share of Total & Conditional Variable Measure
sections.content: Inspect how clean `% of Selected Total` mixes `VAR`, `CALCULATE`, `ALLSELECTED`, and `DIVIDE` cleanly.

codeExamples.code:
Line Revenue = SUMX(FactSales, FactSales[Quantity] * FactSales[UnitPrice])

% Share of Selected Regions = 
VAR CurrentRegionRev = [Line Revenue]
VAR SelectedTotalRev = CALCULATE([Line Revenue], ALLSELECTED(DimRegion))
RETURN
  DIVIDE(CurrentRegionRev, SelectedTotalRev, 0)
codeExamples.explanation: `ALLSELECTED` clears the immediate table row context while respecting the user's report slicer checkboxes.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Accurate % contribution summing cleanly to 100.0% dynamically as external region slicers change

keyPoints: Write base measures (`[Line Revenue]`) once and reuse them inside compound metrics rather than repeating raw `SUM(...)` expressions everywhere.
commonMistakes: Using `ALL(DimRegion)` when you intended dynamic slicer subsets (`ALLSELECTED(DimRegion)`).

exercises.title: Compute Safe Discounted Revenue & % Contribution
exercises.objective: Fix invalid `SUM()` syntax using `SUMX` and build safe `% of Total` ratios.
exercises.description: Refactor broken measure `NetRev = SUM(Orders[Price] * (1 - Orders[DiscountPct]))` and write `% Net Rev of All Categories` ignoring current category row filter.
instructions: Write `% of Categories` dividing `[NetRev]` by `CALCULATE([NetRev], ALL(DimCategory))` cleanly using `DIVIDE`.
exercises.starterCode:
NetRev = ...

Category Share % = 
VAR Cur = [NetRev]
VAR AllCats = ...
RETURN ...
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: `SUMX(Orders, ...)` computes net price per row before summing, and `DIVIDE(Cur, CALCULATE([NetRev], ALL(DimCategory)), 0)` guards safely against empty slices.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why must `Net Sales` across `Quantity * UnitPrice` columns inside a Measure use `SUMX` rather than `SUM`?

options.text: `SUM` accepts only a single column reference without row context; `SUMX` iterates row-by-row over the table evaluating the multiplication

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Row iterators (`SUMX`, `MINX`, `AVERAGEX`) step across row context prior to aggregating.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: How does `ALLSELECTED(Products)` behave inside `CALCULATE()` differently from `ALL(Products)`?

options.text: `ALLSELECTED` restores filters originating from external page/report slicers while clearing visual inner row groupings; `ALL` removes ALL filters unconditionally
Both behave identically in every matrix

knowledgeChecks.explanation: `ALLSELECTED` keeps report-level slicer interactivity accurate on percentages.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why wrap ratios in `DIVIDE(numerator, denominator)` instead of `numerator / denominator`?

options.text: `DIVIDE` gracefully catches zero or blank denominators returning BLANK/fallback without crashing visuals with `Infinity`

recap: You mastered DAX evaluation contexts, X-iterators (`SUMX`), `CALCULATE` filter manipulation, and clean `VAR` structure.
